samples.summary: An array is accepted as a slide `Block`; the `style`/`inlines` repairs land as array expandos that JSON drops, storing exactly the crashing shape the walk exists to prevent
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` guards only with `if (!block || typeof block !== 'object') throw`. `typeof [] === 'object'`, so a body containing `blocks: [[]]` passes. Line 904 then does `block.style = {}` and `normalizeSlideInlines` does `block.inlines = []` — both array expandos, which `JSON.stringify` (and therefore `writeSlidesRoot`'s verbatim persist and the echoed response) drops. The stored block is `[]`, and every reader the diff cites (`ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts, the layout engine's `block.inlines.map`) then throws. The same file rejects arrays for exactly this reason at lines 836 (`assertValidTextBody`), 932 (docs-table cell) and 657 (element `data`) — the block case was missed.

samples.summary: An array is accepted as a nested element (group child / layout placeholder); the `data` repair is an array expando JSON drops, persisting an element with no `data`
samples.evidence: `assertValidNestedElement` guards only `if (!element || typeof element !== 'object') throw`, so `data: { children: [[]] }` (or a layout `placeholders: [[]]`) passes. `assertValidElementData` then hits `raw === undefined` and executes `e.data = emptyElementData(e.type)` on an array (line 663) — an expando that JSON serialization drops. The stored child is `[]`, and per the diff's own rationale the renderer's unconditional `element.data.effects?.shadow` is then a TypeError for every viewer of the deck. Top-level `assertValidElement` is safe only incidentally (it demands string `id`/`type`).

samples.summary: The block/table-cell validation walk recurses without any depth bound, while the sibling element walk added in the same change is bounded by MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH — a compact payload can exhaust the stack
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` (line 888) → docs-table cell → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks(cell, …)` (line 937) → `assertValidSlideBlocks(cell.blocks)` is mutually recursive with no depth parameter. The docs arm's `assertValidBlock` → `tableData.rows[r].cells[c].blocks[cb]` → `assertValidBlock` (line 406) is likewise unbounded, and is now additionally reachable through the newly-validated `header`/`footer` regions. The change explicitly adds `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (line 617) because "the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint"; a deeply nested `tableData` payload reaches the same RangeError through these paths, surfacing as a 500.

samples.summary: A `null` docs-table cell inside a slide text body is skipped rather than repaired, contradicting the null-cell repair the same change adds for slide table elements
samples.evidence: Line 927: `if (cell === undefined || cell === null) continue;`. The slides-table path repairs the identical case at line 800 (`cells[c] = { body: { blocks: [] }, style: {} }`) with the rationale that "the PDF exporter's `for (const cell of row.cells) bodies.push(cell.body)` does not [tolerate a null cell]". A docs table nested inside a slide text body reaches the same docs table renderer/exporter, so a null cell there is stored and crashes those readers.

samples.summary: Docs-arm block `style` accepts an array (typeof [] === 'object'), unlike the slides arm which explicitly rejects it
samples.evidence: Line 376 `if (!b.style || typeof b.style !== 'object')` lets `style: []` through, and `assertValidBlockStyle` then reads only named keys off it, so it validates clean. The slides arm added in this same change rejects an array style explicitly (line 906, `typeof block.style !== 'object' || Array.isArray(block.style)`). The docs writer then serializes no attributes and the reader substitutes defaults, so the impact is a silently discarded style rather than a crash — but the two arms disagree on the same input.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `assertValidSlideBlocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:892) guards only `if (!block || typeof block !== 'object')` with no `Array.isArray` check, so a block entry that is an array passes. The repairs then set expandos on that array: `block.style = {}` (line 904) and `block.inlines = []` in `normalizeSlideInlines` (line 976). `writeSlidesRoot` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (slides-tree.ts:105) and the handler echoes `return body` (line 203) as JSON, and array expandos are dropped by both array→CRDTArray conversion and JSON serialization — so the persisted/echoed block is `[]`. Readers then throw: `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:99) and `block.inlines.map` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:154). Reachable via `slides[*].notes` (line 562, only `Array.isArray(s.notes)` is checked) and via `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (lines 875-880, which validates only that `blocks` is an array, not its entries). The same file rejects arrays for exactly this documented reason at lines 657, 782, 804, 836 and 932, and the docs arm escapes only because `assertValidBlock` demands `b.id` (line 370) — the slide walk deliberately does not. No DTO/class-validator upstream; `@Body() body: unknown` (line 131). Real, unguarded, stores a crashing shape: blocking under the correctness rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `assertValidNestedElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:605-607) tests only `!element || typeof element !== 'object'`, with no `Array.isArray` — so an array passes, unlike every sibling object check in the same file (:782, :804, :813, :836, :906). It is reached with attacker-controlled entries from group children (:708-713) and layout placeholders/staticElements (:512-519). `assertValidElementData` then sees `e.data === undefined` and executes `e.data = emptyElementData(e.type)` at :663, which lands as an Array expando — dropped on serialization/Yorkie assignment. The file's own comment (:642-644) declares arrays must be rejected rather than repaired, but that rule is applied only to `data` (:657), not to the element itself, so the intended invariant has a hole. No guard elsewhere: the PUT handler validates and then passes the identical body to `writeSlidesRoot`, which bulk-assigns `root.layouts` / `root.slides` verbatim (slides-tree.ts:93-110). The persisted `[]` element then crashes readers — `drawElement` destructures `const { frame } = element` and reads `frame.flipH` (element-renderer.ts:175-181) and `element.data.effects?.shadow` (:257) while recursing into group children (:241). Only inaccuracy is which line throws first (frame, not data.effects), which does not affect the outcome. Real, reachable, and blocking (persisted data that crashes every viewer).

finding.summary: The block/table-cell validation walk recurses without any depth bound, while the sibling element walk added in the same change is bounded by MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH — a compact payload can exhaust the stack
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` (line 888) → docs-table cell → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks(cell, …)` (line 937) → `assertValidSlideBlocks(cell.blocks)` is mutually recursive with no depth parameter. The docs arm's `assertValidBlock` → `tableData.rows[r].cells[c].blocks[cb]` → `assertValidBlock` (line 406) is likewise unbounded, and is now additionally reachable through the newly-validated `header`/`footer` regions. The change explicitly adds `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (line 617) because "the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint"; a deeply nested `tableData` payload reaches the same RangeError through these paths, surfacing as a 500.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `assertValidBlock` (docs-content.controller.ts:365) has no depth parameter and self-recurses into table-cell blocks at line 406, reachable from body blocks (line 261) and from the newly-validated header/footer regions (line 296, invoked at 269-270). On the slides side, `assertValidSlideBlocks` (line 888, signature `(blocks, path)` with no depth) walks `block.tableData.rows[r].cells[c]` (lines 919-926) and calls `assertValidTextBodyBlocks(cell, cellPath)` at line 937, which calls back to `assertValidSlideBlocks` at line 880 — an unbounded mutual recursion. The sibling element walk in the same file IS bounded (`assertValidElementData` line 646 checks `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` at lines 651-655, MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH=32 at line 617), and its own comment names the threat: a 25 MB JSON body limit, which is real (main.ts:20 '25mb', applied main.ts:49-50). The depth counter is threaded only through `data.children` (line 712) and never reaches the tableData walks. No other guard exists: the only depth test (spec:1573-1588) exercises group `children` nesting only, and validation runs before any type lookup in the PUT handler (lines 147-159), so the path is reachable on an authenticated request. Unbounded recursion producing a RangeError/500 on a reachable path is a missing-guard crash squarely in the correctness lane; nothing supports not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
